title: Accounts Assistant
company: Hays Specialist Recruitment Limited - Agency - Permanent
description:
Accounts Assistant

Location: Derry
Salary: £30,000- £35,000 depending on experience
Hours: Full-time, office-based

Your new company

You will be joining an established and growing organisation with a diverse portfolio of operations across the UK and Ireland. This is a fantastic opportunity to become part of a friendly, down-to-earth finance team where you will be given responsibility, variety and the opportunity to develop your accounting experience.The company offers a collaborative working environment where people are trusted to get on with their work, contribute ideas and play an important part in the continued growth of the organisation.

Your new role

As Accounts Assistant, you will support the day-to-day finance function across a number of group companies. This is a varied position and would particularly suit someone who enjoys having exposure to different areas of finance rather than focusing solely on one transactional function.
Your responsibilities will include:
- Maintaining computerised accounting records across several group companies
- Processing and maintaining the purchase and sales ledgers
- Completing regular bank reconciliations
- Assisting with supplier payment runs and resolving queries
- Completing intercompany reconciliations
- Preparing and submitting VAT returns
- Supporting the preparation of management accounts and year-end accounts
- Assisting with project costings
- Maintaining accurate financial records
- Providing general accounts and administrative support to the wider finance team

This is an excellent opportunity for someone who wants to build on their existing accounts experience and gain broader exposure within a busy finance environment.

What you'll need to succeed

You will ideally have previous experience as an Accounts Assistant, Assistant Accountant, Accounts Technician or similar finance position.
You will also have:
- Previous hands-on experience across areas such as purchase ledger, sales ledger and reconciliations
- Strong numerical skills with excellent attention to detail
- Good organisational skills and the ability to manage competing deadlines
- Confidence working both independently and as part of a wider team
- Good Microsoft Excel and general IT skills
- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills
- A proactive, positive approach to your work
- Experience using Sage Accounts 50 would be advantageous
- An Accounting Technician qualification or someone part-qualified in ACA/ACCA or similar would be advantageous, although relevant practical accounts experience will also be considered.

What you'll get in return

You will receive a competitive salary and benefits package along with the opportunity to join a supportive and approachable finance team.Most importantly, this is a role that offers genuine variety and development. You will gain exposure across several areas of accounting and work across multiple group companies, making it a strong opportunity for someone looking to broaden their experience and progress their finance career.

What you need to do now

If you're interested in this role, please submit your most up-to-date CV for consideration.If this job isn't quite right for you, but you are considering a new opportunity within Accountancy & Finance in Derry and the North West, please get in touch for a confidential discussion about your career.

title: Credit Control
description:
Consula is recruiting on behalf of an international facilities and property services business with its head office in London for an organised and confident Credit Controller.

Our client has built a strong reputation for reliable service and long-standing customer relationships, and as the business continues to grow, they are strengthening their finance team with a credit control specialist who can protect cash flow while keeping customers on side.

In this role, you will own a ledger serving a large portfolio of commercial, retail and public sector accounts. You will be the friendly, persistent voice that keeps accounts up to date, resolving queries quickly and making sure payments arrive on time. Your work has a direct impact on the business's cash position, its customer relationships and the accuracy of month-end reporting.

The office is a short walk from major Underground and rail connections, with hybrid working available once you are settled into the role.

Location: London

Salary: £39,000 - £43,000 per year

Employment: Permanent

THE ROLE

As Credit Controller, you will manage the full collections cycle for your ledger, working closely with sales, customer service and the wider finance team.
- Managing a designated sales ledger, chasing overdue balances by telephone and email in a professional, solution-focused way.
- Prioritising collections activity using aged debt reports to reduce debtor days and keep overdue balances under control.
- Investigating and resolving invoice queries, disputes and pricing discrepancies with internal teams.
- Setting up and monitoring payment plans, and escalating persistent non-payment in line with credit policy.
- Allocating cash receipts and reconciling customer accounts accurately and promptly.
- Carrying out credit checks on new and existing customers and recommending appropriate credit limits.
- Placing accounts on stop where required and communicating clearly with account managers.
- Preparing weekly cash forecasts and aged debt reports for the Finance Manager.
- Supporting month-end close, audit requests and continuous improvement of the credit control process.

ABOUT YOU

Our client is keen to meet people who are calm under pressure, persuasive on the phone and meticulous with detail.

Essential:
- Proven experience in credit control, collections or accounts receivable.
- Confident, courteous telephone manner with the resilience to handle difficult conversations.
- Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage a high volume of accounts at once.
- Good working knowledge of Excel, including filters, lookups and pivot tables.
- High standards of accuracy when allocating cash and reconciling accounts.

Desirable:
- Experience of accounting systems such as Sage, Xero, SAP, Dynamics or similar.
- Understanding of credit checking tools and the debt recovery process.
- AAT or CICM qualification, or working towards one.

A TYPICAL DAY

You will start the morning by reviewing yesterday's receipts, allocating cash and checking which accounts are now due or overdue. Mid-morning is focused on your call list, speaking with customers, agreeing payment dates and logging every conversation. In the afternoon you will chase up outstanding queries with colleagues in sales and operations, review credit applications and update your aged debt report, finishing the day with a clear plan of priorities for tomorrow.

WHAT YOU CAN EXPECT
- A secure, permanent role within an established and supportive London finance team.
- Hybrid working once you are settled into the role.
- 28 days' annual leave including bank holidays.
- Workplace pension scheme with employer contributions.
- Study support towards AAT or CICM qualifications for the right person.
- Structured induction and clear progression routes within the finance function.
- A friendly team culture with regular recognition of good work.
- Health and wellbeing support, including an employee assistance programme.

If you are a determined, organised credit control professional looking for your next step, we would be delighted to hear from you. Apply through Consula today and Doug, our AI talent partner, will be in touch to discuss the role further.

title: Credit Control
description:
You will be empowered to manage collections across an allocated client portfolio, prioritising by value and age of debt, while collaborating closely with partners and client-facing teams.

The organisation is committed to training opportunities and knowledge-sharing, ensuring you have access to ongoing support from experienced colleagues and supportive leadership.

What You'll Do:

As a Credit Controller, your day-to-day responsibilities will centre around managing collections for an assigned portfolio of clients. You will be instrumental in agreeing payment plans, escalating overdue accounts when necessary, and collaborating with various internal teams to resolve billing queries. Your analytical skills will be put to use as you monitor aged debt positions, produce regular reporting on debtor status and cash collections, recommend provisions for bad debts, and identify emerging trends or risks within the debtor book. You will also play a key role in setting credit limits for clients, supporting credit checks for new business relationships, ensuring consistent application of payment terms, and contributing ideas for process improvements-especially those involving automation. Success in this role means reducing debtor days, minimising bad debt write-offs, achieving cash collection targets, and delivering accurate reporting-all while maintaining positive relationships with clients and colleagues.

Manage collections across an allocated client portfolio by prioritising accounts based on value and age of debt to ensure timely payments.

Agree payment plans with clients and escalate overdue or disputed accounts according to established credit control policies.

Collaborate with partners and client-facing teams to resolve billing queries efficiently and prevent future disputes.

Provide cover across the full debtor ledger during periods of absence, ensuring continuity of service within the finance department.

Monitor the aged debt position regularly and produce comprehensive debtor and cash collection reports for management review.

Recommend bad debt provisions and write-offs for approval by senior stakeholders based on thorough analysis of the debtor book.

Identify trends and risks within the debtor portfolio and propose actionable recommendations to mitigate potential issues.

Set and review client credit limits as well as support credit checks for new clients to maintain robust credit management practices.

Ensure terms of business and payment terms are applied consistently across all client accounts to uphold organisational standards.

Contribute to process improvement initiatives by helping enhance credit control policies, processes, systems, including automation tools.

What You'll Bring:

The ideal candidate for the Credit Controller position brings substantial experience managing client portfolios within credit control environments. Your interpersonal skills enable you to negotiate payment plans effectively while maintaining positive relationships with clients. You possess strong analytical abilities demonstrated through regular production of aged debt reports and collections analysis. Proficiency in Excel combined with experience using accounting systems allows you to manage financial data efficiently. Your organisational skills ensure that records are kept meticulously up-to-date while your attention to detail supports accurate reporting. Clear communication is vital; you excel at conveying information professionally both verbally and in writing. Experience working collaboratively within small teams showcases your commitment to knowledge-sharing. Industry-specific experience within professional services is valued but not mandatory; similarly CICM qualifications or familiarity with automated collections software would further strengthen your profile. Above all else, your dependability ensures that you provide reliable cover across the debtor ledger whenever needed.

Substantial experience in credit control is essential, including proven ability to manage a portfolio of client accounts effectively.

Your negotiation skills are highly developed, enabling you to agree payment plans confidently with clients as well as senior internal stakeholders.

Experience producing aged debt reports and collections reporting demonstrates your analytical capabilities within finance functions.

Proficiency in Excel alongside familiarity with accounting systems ensures you can handle data accurately and efficiently.

You are well organised with strong attention to detail which supports accurate record-keeping and timely reporting.

Clear communication skills both written and verbal allow you to interact professionally with clients and colleagues alike.

Experience working as part of a small team highlights your collaborative approach and willingness to share knowledge.

Credit control experience within professional services is desirable as it provides valuable industry insight.

CICM qualification or progress towards it would be advantageous for further professional development.

Familiarity with automated collections or credit control software is beneficial for supporting process improvements.

Combined Calendar
Set up and run one calendar for the whole business, with reminders far enough ahead to act on:
- Accounts: VAT returns, annual accounts, confirmation statements and payroll dates, each with a preparation window before it.
- Property: rent due dates, rent reviews, lease breaks and expiries, and tenancy renewals.
- Compliance: gas safety, electrical, fire risk, EPC and other certificates, licences and inspections.
- Insurance: renewal dates.
- People: HR dates such as probation reviews and annual reviews.

Insurance Admin
- Keep the insurance schedule up to date: policies, renewal dates, premiums and documents.
- Be the brokers' day-to-day contact for documents, changes and renewals.
- Tell the brokers in writing about changes such as vacant units, changes of use and building works, as directed.
- Keep the claims file in order.
- Review policy documents and make sure their terms and conditions are kept to, for example inspections of vacant units, heating and water rules, tenant referencing and electrical safety reports. Diarise each condition and flag anything not being met.

Office, Post and Records
- Clear the backlog of paper records in the office: sort, scan where useful, file, and send to storage.
- Set up and keep a retention and destruction schedule for stored records, on the accountant's advice.
- Keep the office running: supplies, equipment, deliveries and visitors.
- Help with the office move in May 2027.

Company and Legal Administration
- Keep company records up to date for the four companies and prepare Companies House filings for approval.
- Keep registers of leases, tenancies, licences and key documents, and know where the originals are.

HR Admin
- Keep staff files: contracts, right-to-work checks, holiday and absence records.
- Diarise probation and annual reviews, and help prepare them.
- Help with recruitment admin: adverts, CVs, interview scheduling and onboarding.
- Keep HR policies filed and up to date, with the HR adviser.

IT & Systems
- Be the day-to-day contact for the IT provider: new users, laptops, access and faults.
- Help move files into the new shared document system and keep its folders tidy.

Supporting the team
- Support Associate Director with diary management, meeting notes, trackers and document preparation.
- Support the Property Manager, with document chasing, filing and tenancy paperwork. Keep the property management software, Konnexions, fully up to date and well managed: tenants, leases, rents, deposits, certificates, contacts and documents. The team needs all the information there to be accurate and current, because they rely on it to manage the portfolio.
- Work with the Liverpool team on shared admin tasks.

Skills and Experience Required:
- Minimum 5 years' experience in office or accounts administration within property
- Be confident with Xero and Excel
- Experience with property management software
- Excellent accuracy and attention to detail
- AAT Level 2 or equivalent bookkeeping knowledge

- Working closely with the Managing Director, advising and updating on all matters relating to credit control and the debtor position

- Agreeing payment plans with clients where appropriate
- Achieving agreed targets for debtor days and overall debt value, and reporting regularly on performance against them

The rewards
As a progressive, responsible company, they are committed to supporting employees work life balance. The role of Credit Controller is a fully remote position and the hours of work are 20 hours per week, Monday to Friday, with flexible working hours within reason.
- The salary on offer is £30,000 to £32,000 per annum FTE, depending on experience (£15,000 £16,000 actual for 0.5 FTE)
